claims.text: Adding graphene nanoplatelets to a W–Cu composite will increase its thermal conductivity.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will retain mechanical durability under heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor conditions.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will retain irradiation resistance under fusion-reactor conditions.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of 0.5–2.0 vol% graphene nanoplatelets during W–Cu composite processing.
The proposed operating range extends to approximately 1000°C.
The expected behavior applies under irradiation levels typical of fusion-reactor joint and heat-dissipation applications.
Processing with graphene nanoplatelets will produce a uniform nanoplatelet dispersion.
The dispersed graphene nanoplatelets will form interconnected pathways in the metal matrix.
Interconnected graphene pathways will improve phonon-mediated heat transport in the W–Cu composite.
Graphene nanoplatelets have high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Graphene nanoplatelets will act as thermal bridges across tungsten–copper interfaces.
Graphene bridges across tungsten–copper interfaces will reduce thermal boundary resistance.
Graphene incorporation at the proposed loading will not disrupt microstructural factors responsible for mechanical durability.
Graphene incorporation at the proposed loading will not disrupt microstructural factors responsible for irradiation resistance.
The graphene-modified composite will have approximately 10–20% higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable graphene-free W–Cu composite.
The mechanical properties of the graphene-modified composite will remain comparable to those of the graphene-free baseline.
The irradiation resistance of the graphene-modified composite will remain comparable to that of the graphene-free baseline.
The expected benefits may not occur outside the 0.5–2.0 vol% graphene range or under substantially different operating conditions.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thermal-conductivity increase, or significant degradation of mechanical durability or irradiation resistance, would falsify the hypothesis.
